verification.note: Reproduced by reading the code. frontend/e2e-components/fixture-origin.spec.ts:13 defines ACROSS_DOCUMENTS = /\.reload\(|\.go(Back|Forward)\(|\bcontext(\(\))?\.newPage\(/. It has no alternative that matches a repeated page.goto, so a spec that writes localStorage and then calls open() or page.goto again on file:// would not be picked up by the filter at line 22, and the guard would pass. Line 20 filters only names ending in .spec.ts, so *.cases.ts helpers are never scanned. scenes-section-rows.cases.ts:43-47 writes localStorage through addInitScript, which confirms that helpers outside the scan do touch storage. Both migrated specs navigate through page.goto inside open() (player-workbench-desktop.spec.ts:63, workbench-split-desktop.spec.ts:62; workbench-split-desktop.spec.ts:1193 has another goto). I found no current file:// spec that crosses documents through a repeated goto, so the gap is latent, as the finding says.

specification_compliance: The guard's doc comment at fixture-origin.spec.ts:12 lists reload, history navigation and a second page. A repeated goto is not in that list, so the guard covers less than its stated purpose at line 2 ('reads localStorage across documents').
potential_unspecified_behavior: Whether a repeated page.goto on file:// actually loses or shares localStorage under the browsers in use was not determined. That decides whether the gap can ever make a test flaky.
regression_risks: A future spec that stays on file:// and crosses documents through a second goto, or through a .cases.ts helper, would pass the guard while still exposed to the original flakiness.
test_coverage: fixture-origin.spec.ts is a static source scan. It covers only the four patterns in ACROSS_DOCUMENTS and only *.spec.ts files.
not_verified: I did not run the Playwright suite or the guard test.
I did not check every file:// spec test by test for multiple goto calls after a storage write; I only grepped for goto, storage and navigation sites.
I did not check whether .cases.ts helpers are imported by file:// specs in a way that crosses documents.
